title: review: E1 fix round 1 (v2): security_paths cover the MCP surface, prompts and skills; NUL-safe diff; real git tests; empty list fails closed (from review T-0221)
spec:
Fix round on task/T-0220 (commit d8531a3, which sits on goal/T-0201 head 6358799). STEP 0, before anything else: your worktree was cut from goal/T-0201 and lacks that commit. Run `git reset --hard task/T-0220` in the worktree and confirm `git log --oneline -1` shows d8531a3; then work on top of it. Address the opus review T-0221 on orchestrator/daemon.py, .orchestrator/pool.toml and tests/test_daemon.py:
1. pool.toml [review] security_paths adds orchestrator/mcp.py, orchestrator/bus_mcp.py, .orchestrator/prompts/**, skills/**, .claude/skills/**, .mcp.worker.json. Keep orchestrator/jev*.py with a comment that E2 (T-0214) adds the files. Mirror the same list in DEFAULT_SECURITY_PATHS.
2. changed_paths(): run git diff --name-only -z <base>..HEAD and split on NUL so quoted or non-ASCII paths match the globs; still None on any failure.
3. _review_plan(): under code_review="security_paths" an empty or missing security_paths list fails closed: one review with review_reason 'security_paths_empty' and a one-time notify, never a silent "none".
4. Tests over a real temporary git repo (init, commit on a goal/<parent> branch, cut a task branch, commit): a change under .claude/hooks/ matches; a change to a plain source file does not; a path with a space and an umlaut matches through -z; a non-git worktree returns None; empty security_paths yields reviews_expected 1 with review_reason security_paths_empty. Keep the monkeypatched tests as they are.
Out of scope: CLAUDE.md / planner.md / README wording (T-0213 E1b does that after this merges). Commit on your task branch when green.
acceptance: git log on the task branch contains d8531a3 (E1 v2) below the fix commit
pool.toml security_paths contains orchestrator/mcp.py, orchestrator/bus_mcp.py, .orchestrator/prompts/**, skills/**, .claude/skills/**
All tests from T-0220 still pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: changed_paths() runs `git diff --name-only -z` with git's default rename detection on, and --name-only prints only the NEW path for a rename. Verified in a scratch repo: `git mv .claude/hooks/a.sh moved.sh` yields exactly `moved.sh`. So renaming a guarded file out of a security glob (disabling .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh, moving orchestrator/merge.py) produces a diff matching nothing, _review_plan() returns (0,"none") and gate() auto-merges it unreviewed. A plain delete is caught (old path is printed); a rename is not. This defeats the fail-closed intent T-0221 was written for. Fix is one flag: add --no-renames (or -M0) to the diff invocation, and add a rename test alongside test_changed_paths_quoted_path_matches.

The `security` flag covers only "diff_unavailable" and "security_paths:*", so the third fail-closed reason, "security_paths_empty", falls through to the code_review=="always" branch. Its review is created with tier=review_tier(t) and complexity=t["complexity"] unbumped, so it never gets spawn.py's >=7 security checklist and does not honour security_review_tier — contrary to _review_plan()'s docstring, which presents all three as the same fail-closed outcome. test_empty_security_paths_fails_closed only asserts len(reviews)==1, so it passes without noticing.

security_paths enumerates orchestrator modules individually and omits two that are security-relevant: orchestrator/__init__.py (defines ROOT/STATE, i.e. where protected-paths.txt, pool.toml and the bus live) and orchestrator/cli.py (entry point wiring daemon/merge/install/serve). Under the new security_paths default a change to either merges with zero review. Consider `orchestrator/*.py` with explicit exclusions, or add these two.
